text:
alex: Heads up — at 21:37 UTC we saw a surge of node flaps in eu-west-1 that triggered an affinity rollback. A bunch of tenants fell back to the default pool and p95 gen latency spiked ~3x. Logs: ```node=gpu-node-42 event=flap:link_down; routing=affinity_rollback tenant=acme-corp -> default_pool``` Can we try a short-term mitigation: add an `affinity_grace: 30s` to avoid immediate rollback and route latency-sensitive tenants to a `fallback_microdedicated` pool instead of default? @sam @maya
sam: Seen it too. I also noticed disk IO peaking on gpu-node-42 right before the flap. +1 on grace timer, but concerned: fallback_microdedicated might exhaust capacity and cause preemptions. Can we enforce `per_tenant_max=2` on that pool (max concurrent slices) and `max_burst=1`? Also need to ensure KV cache isn't duplicated.
maya: Agreed. I'll canary a routing rule for eu-west-slot-3 for 30m. Proposed rule (will push as canary): ```yaml
routing:
  rule: if tenant.qos == "latency-sensitive" and node.region == "eu-west-1" then route: fallback_microdedicated
  fallback_policy:
    affinity_grace_seconds: 30
    per_tenant_max_slices: 2
    max_burst_slices: 1
``` infra-bot: deploy | routing-rule v2026.3 started by maya — canary(target=eu-west-slot-3) queued
alex: Thanks. Key metrics to watch during canary: `p95_generation_latency`, `queue_depth`, `preemptions_count`, `kv_cache_misses`. Alert if p95 > 300ms OR preemptions > 5 in 10m. I'll add a temporary dashboard and alert rule.
sam: One more thing — cost impact. fallback_microdedicated uses reserved commit but bursts over commit will go to on-demand billing. If this runs for 24h with current load we estimate ~18% incremental GPU cost for that AZ. Keep an eye on billing export.
maya: Starting canary now, will watch alerts and rollback if preemptions spike. @ryan FYI (oncall) — please watch infra-sentry for any new I/O or NIC errors. :eyes:
